t: Formed on 22 May 1990 by the union of the conservative Yemen Arab Republic and the Marxist South Yemen.
A brief democratic opening gave way to the 1994 civil war and Saleh's long rule through tribal and military patronage.
Since the Houthis seized Sanaa in 2014 it has been torn by war and one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.
dyk: In 1990 Yemen sat on the UN Security Council and voted against the resolution authorising force against Iraq, a stand that cost hundreds of thousands of Yemenis their jobs in Saudi Arabia.
ev: North and South Yemen unite as the Republic of Yemen on 22 May
Northern forces defeat a southern secession and take Aden
Treaty of Jeddah fixes the Saudi border; al-Qaeda bombs the USS Cole in Aden
The first of six wars against the Houthi movement begins in Saada
Mass protests force Saleh to agree to hand over power
A Saudi-led coalition intervenes in the war
A Presidential Leadership Council takes over the recognised government

f.capital: Sanaa; recognised government based in Aden since 2015
f.founder: Ali Abdullah Saleh and Ali Salim al-Beidh
f.predecessor: Yemen Arab Republic and South Yemen
